items.title: Implement account recovery, reverification and session revocation
items.outcome: A user who has lost their passkey or device can regain access through recovery codes or channel reverification, under a cooling-off window, and every recovery revokes existing sessions and devices, so recovery is a controlled path rather than the weakest link in authentication.
items.context: Passkey-first authentication moves the entire risk of the system onto the recovery path: an attacker does not break the passkey, they claim to have lost it. T-ADR-AUTH-05 decides the provider, the relying-party identifier and the recovery model, and nothing implements the decision. Today registration and login exist in api#4 and api#5 and recovery exists nowhere, which means the first user who changes phones is unrecoverable and the first attacker who social-engineers support is unstoppable.
scope: Recovery code issuance at enrolment: single-use codes, hashed at rest, count and regeneration rules
Channel reverification as the second recovery route, with the channel proven at enrolment rather than at recovery time
Cooling-off window between an accepted recovery attempt and the credential change taking effect, with notification to every registered channel
Cancellation path so the legitimate owner can stop a recovery in progress during the cooling-off window
Session and device revocation on successful recovery, including refresh-token families
Rate limits and lockout on recovery attempts, separate from the login rate limits
Audit events for every recovery attempt, acceptance, cancellation and completion
Anti-enumeration behaviour so the response does not reveal whether an account, a channel or a code exists
acceptance_criteria: A user with a valid unused recovery code completes recovery and can authenticate again, and the code cannot be used a second time
Recovery codes are stored hashed; a database read yields no usable code, proven by a test
A recovery attempt starts a cooling-off window of the published length, notifies every registered channel, and does not change any credential until the window elapses
Cancelling during the cooling-off window aborts the recovery and leaves every existing credential and session intact
Completing recovery revokes every active session, every refresh-token family and every registered device, proven by a test that replays a pre-recovery refresh token and asserts rejection
Recovery attempts are rate limited and locked out independently of login, proven by a test that exhausts recovery attempts without locking normal login for other users
Responses to recovery initiation are identical for an existing and a non-existing account, in body, status and timing band, proven by an enumeration test
Every recovery attempt, cancellation and completion writes an audit event carrying the route used and the outcome
Channel reverification uses only a channel proven at enrolment; a channel added during the recovery flow is refused
contracts_schema: Recovery initiation, verification, cancellation and completion published in the OpenAPI document with generated clients and contract verification
Recovery route is an enumerated value in the contract, so a client cannot invent a third route
security_privacy: No recovery response distinguishes an existing account from a non-existing one, including by timing band
Recovery codes are never logged, never returned after issuance and never retrievable
A completed recovery is treated as a credential compromise event: sessions, devices and refresh families are all revoked rather than selectively kept
The cooling-off notification is the control that makes a silent account takeover visible to the legitimate owner
observability: Recovery initiation, acceptance, cancellation and completion rates are recorded, and an unusual initiation rate raises an alert
Lockout events are recorded with the reason so a support request can be answered without inspecting the database
tests: Recovery-specific rate limit and lockout test
Account enumeration test covering body, status and timing band
rollout_rollback: Recovery is enabled behind a flag and exercised end to end in staging before any real account exists
Rollback disables the recovery routes and leaves login and registration untouched; no credential state is migrated by this ticket
non_goals: Support-operated manual account recovery, which requires the support intake and verification path in T-SUP-01 and the administrative controls in E13
Client recovery screens, which T-AUTH-02 owns for Android and T-WEB-01 owns for web
Choosing the authentication provider or the relying-party identifier, which T-ADR-AUTH-05 decides
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the recovery endpoints, the code store, the cooling-off timer and the revocation cascade. Clients consume the published contract and own no recovery logic of their own.
definition_of_done: Merged only after a current-head core-reviewer attestation from a separate qualified reviewer-agent session
Every acceptance criterion demonstrated by a named automated test or attached evidence
Tests listed in this ticket run in CI, and their check names and the local commands that reproduce them are recorded for T-SCA-INF-01
Observability, rollout and rollback notes recorded on the ticket before merge
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Build the Android recovery, lost-device and re-enrolment journey
items.outcome: An Android user who has lost their device or their passkey can start recovery, understand the cooling-off window, cancel a recovery they did not start, and re-enrol a credential on a new device, without contacting support.
items.context: The server-side recovery path in T-AUTH-01 is unusable without a client surface, and the lost-device case is precisely the case where the user does not have the app they are being asked to open. The journey therefore has to work on a fresh install on a new device, and it has to make the cooling-off window and the cancellation option understandable, because the cancellation notification is the only defence a legitimate owner has against a silent takeover.
scope: Recovery entry point reachable before authentication, on a fresh install
Recovery code entry and channel reverification routes, presented as a choice with their consequences stated
Cooling-off state surface: what is happening, when it completes, and how to cancel
Cancellation journey reachable from the notification, working on a device that is not enrolled
Credential re-enrolment on the new device after recovery completes
Recovery code storage guidance at enrolment, including regeneration
Every state from the T-UX-01 taxonomy that applies: loading, error, offline, permission-denied and degraded
acceptance_criteria: Recovery can be started from a fresh install with no existing session, proven by an instrumented test on a clean profile
The two recovery routes are presented with their real consequences, and the screen never claims recovery is instant when a cooling-off window applies
The cooling-off screen shows the completion time and a working cancellation action, and the cancellation action succeeds from a device that has never been enrolled
Re-enrolment on the new device completes and the previous device's session is shown as revoked
Recovery codes are never rendered into a screenshot-eligible surface without an explicit user action, and are never written to logs
Every applicable T-UX-01 state identifier is handled on every recovery screen, asserted by the client state coverage check
The journey is accessible under TalkBack and passes the accessibility budget applied to the other core journeys
contracts_schema: Consumes the published recovery contract from T-AUTH-01 through the generated client; no recovery endpoint is called by hand-written request code
security_privacy: Recovery codes are not stored on the device after use and are excluded from backup and autofill
The recovery screens reveal nothing about whether an account exists for an entered identifier
Screenshots are suppressed on the recovery code surface
observability: Client records recovery start, route chosen, cancellation and completion so drop-off in the journey is visible
tests: Cancellation-from-notification test on an unenrolled device
Screenshot suppression and log-absence test for recovery codes
State coverage test against the T-UX-01 identifiers
rollout_rollback: Shipped behind the same flag as the server routes, enabled together in staging first
Rollback hides the client entry point; the server routes remain and no local state is migrated
non_goals: Server-side recovery logic, which T-AUTH-01 owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo android. Owns the recovery, cooling-off, cancellation and re-enrolment screens. The contract and every server rule belong to T-AUTH-01.
